scope: Restores keyboard email operation announcements, allows subject-only or body-only sending, removes the startup speech wait, and shortens setting-change feedback. This is a beta testing build.

topics.title: Subject-only and body-only email
details: A valid recipient and either a subject or a body are sufficient to review a new message. The review explicitly says no subject or no message body when that part is blank. An entirely empty message is still refused.

For voice composition, say skip subject, no subject, or leave subject blank to move from the subject to the body. A response keeps the original message subject. The guided recipient, subject and body workflow, review and Yes/No confirmation remain available. Alt+S and Ctrl+Enter still start the same review.

topics.title: Email operation announcements with the keyboard
details: Getting messages from the selected folder and Email sent successfully bypass the navigation speech coalescing that previously discarded them. Progress starts before fetching. Before the final folder summary, active status speech can complete; rapid navigation continues to retain only the latest ordinary destination feedback.

The local keyboard speech worker now marks speech active when it actually starts, so send success is not immediately replaced by refresh feedback. Success is announced only after provider acceptance; failure and uncertain-result protections remain in place.

topics.title: Interruptible startup
details: The main input loop no longer waits up to 15 seconds for the startup announcement or discards microphone audio collected during it. The window context is ready for keyboard navigation immediately after the startup update check. Saying Wake up interrupts the current announcement before continuing to the main menu or the previous activity.

The short startup message avoids speaking the literal wake phrase, which could otherwise wake the app through its own speakers. Microphone, model and account initialization still must complete before commands can be processed. Live microphone testing is still needed.

topics.title: Shorter setting-change feedback
details: Tab focus still announces the setting name and current value. Changing a list choice or checkbox announces only its new value, such as medium, 3, on or off. Combo-box child focus is normalized to avoid a second full-label announcement. Category navigation, explicit voice setting requests, OK and Cancel remain unchanged.

Regression checks cover partial email bodies, guided subject skipping, keyboard status announcements before refresh, active local speech, wake interruption and native Windows value-only choice/checkbox feedback. HTML message reading and its saved format preference are unchanged in this build.
